newsitem.title: USA: OLYMPICS-SALT LAKE CHIEF GETS PROBATION.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-SALT LAKE CHIEF GETS PROBATION.

text.p: Tom Welch, the man who toiled for 10 years to bring the Winter Olympic Games to Salt Lake City, pleaded no contest on Thursday to a charge he beat his wife, a clerk of the court said.
Welch's court appearance came a day after Winter Olympic Games organisers agreed to pay him a lump sum of $1 million in connection with his resignation amid the wife-beating scandal.
State court Judge Sheila McCleve also ordered Welch to undergo counselling, the clerk said.
Police were called to the Welch home on July 9 after his wife Alma, 46, claimed he had struck her.

On Tuesday, Welch resigned as President and Chief Operating Officer of the Salt Lake Organising Committee for the Olympic Winter Games of 2002, blaming the stresses of his job for breaking up his marriage.

The next day the trustees of the Salt Lake Organising Committee in a closed-door meeting approved a resolution giving him the $1 million lump sum and also voted to retain him as a consultant at $10,000 a month until the Games take place. He was also awarded a pension of up to $500,000.
Welch is a former Mormon bishop known in Utah as "Mr Olympics."

According to police, Welch was charged with domestic violence battery, based on allegations he bruised and restrained his wife during an argument over another woman. His wife did not press charges but the authorities decided to go ahead with the case.

Welch had worked since 1985 to bring the Winter Olympics to Utah. It lost out to Nagano, Japan, for the 1998 Games before landing the 2002 Games. He was named president and chief executive of the organising committee in 1995.
But even his dedicated efforts did not help him after the scandal broke.

The Deseret News, which is owned by the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and reflects Mormon attitudes, said in an editorial on Wednesday that the need to maintain the ultra-clean image was paramount.
